Symptom: Repeated rattling or clattering sound
Remedy / Action: Stop and inspect the gear set; replace damaged gears after confirming the fault
Source: StepperOnline, “Gearbox - Troubleshooting Guide,” updated 2026, https://help.omc-stepperonline.com/hc/s/articles/gearbox-troubleshooting-guide

Symptom: Rhythmic knocking or clicking once per shaft revolution
Remedy / Action: Shut the unit down; do not keep running; inspect through the cover and replace the damaged gear
Measurable condition: Large wear particles in oil or on the magnetic plug
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Rhythmic knocking or clicking once per shaft revolution
Remedy / Action: Shut down and inspect the coupling; replace worn or loose elements
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Rhythmic knocking or clicking once per shaft revolution
Remedy / Action: Inspect the keyway and shaft; repair or replace
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Rhythmic knocking or clicking once per shaft revolution
Cause / Fault: Foreign object in the housing or cracked tooth or broken bearing cage (clicking every few revolutions)
Remedy / Action: Shut down; check the oil and magnetic plug for metal; plan an internal inspection
Measurable condition: Metal particles on the magnetic plug or in the oil sample
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Steady unusual noise while the gearbox runs
Remedy / Action: Inspect the bearings and replace damaged ones
Source: StepperOnline, “Gearbox - Troubleshooting Guide,” updated 2026, https://help.omc-stepperonline.com/hc/s/articles/gearbox-troubleshooting-guide

Symptom: Steady unusual noise while the gearbox runs
Remedy / Action: Check lubricant condition; renew the oil as appropriate
Source: StepperOnline, “Gearbox - Troubleshooting Guide,” updated 2026, https://help.omc-stepperonline.com/hc/s/articles/gearbox-troubleshooting-guide

Symptom: Intermittent noise from inside the gearbox
Cause / Fault: Debris or foreign particle contacting a gear surface
Remedy / Action: Inspect accessible gear surfaces and remove the contamination using the approved procedure
Source: StepperOnline, “Gearbox - Troubleshooting Guide,” updated 2026, https://help.omc-stepperonline.com/hc/s/articles/gearbox-troubleshooting-guide

Symptom: High-pitched whine or squeal
Remedy / Action: Check the oil level and specified grade; refill only to the maker level
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: High-pitched whine or squeal
Remedy / Action: Investigate gear contact pattern if noise remains
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: High-pitched whine or squeal
Remedy / Action: Check backlash against the maker specification
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: High-pitched whine or squeal
Cause / Fault: Tooth scoring from lubricant film breakdown
Remedy / Action: Verify oil grade, level and sump temperature; inspect the teeth
Measurable condition: Sump oil temperature above 200 F (about 93 C); normal range is 130-180 F
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: High-pitched whine or squeal
Cause / Fault: Oil viscosity too low for the operating temperature
Remedy / Action: Confirm the oil grade and viscosity match the nameplate
Measurable condition: Viscosity drift of more than 10% from the new-oil specification
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: High-pitched whine or squeal
Cause / Fault: Internal misalignment shifting the tooth contact pattern
Remedy / Action: Check alignment and compare the vibration spectrum to the baseline
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Grinding or rough rumble
Cause / Fault: Bearing race or rolling element damage
Remedy / Action: Pull an oil sample and take an envelope vibration spectrum; plan a shutdown and replace the bearing
Measurable condition: Bearing defect frequencies in the vibration spectrum
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Grinding or rough rumble
Remedy / Action: Pull an oil sample; plan an internal inspection and gear replacement
Measurable condition: Rising iron and PQ index in oil analysis
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Grinding or rough rumble
Cause / Fault: Oil contaminated with coarse wear particles
Remedy / Action: Pull an oil sample, find the particle source, then flush and renew the oil
Measurable condition: Particle count worse than ISO 4406 code 19/17/14 (splash systems)
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Siren, warble or hissing sound from the gearbox
Cause / Fault: Bearing in advanced wear or lubricant starvation (siren or warble)
Remedy / Action: Verify lubrication pressure and flow; inspect and replace the bearing
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Siren, warble or hissing sound from the gearbox
Cause / Fault: Blocked suction strainer or lube pump cavitation (hiss)
Remedy / Action: Inspect strainers, check for air on suction lines and verify lube pressure and flow
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Siren, warble or hissing sound from the gearbox
Cause / Fault: Oil level too low on a splash-lubricated unit (hiss)
Remedy / Action: Check and correct the oil level
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Gearbox vibrates noticeably at its mounting base
Remedy / Action: Level the mounting surface and secure the gearbox
Source: StepperOnline, “Gearbox - Troubleshooting Guide,” updated 2026, https://help.omc-stepperonline.com/hc/s/articles/gearbox-troubleshooting-guide

Symptom: Gearbox vibrates noticeably at its mounting base
Remedy / Action: Check mounting alignment and re-mount correctly
Source: StepperOnline, “Gearbox - Troubleshooting Guide,” updated 2026, https://help.omc-stepperonline.com/hc/s/articles/gearbox-troubleshooting-guide

Symptom: Gearbox vibrates noticeably at its mounting base
Remedy / Action: Check soft foot at every hold-down point and shim as needed
Measurable condition: Vibration velocity above 4.5 mm/s RMS (ISO 10816 Class III zone C limit)
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Output shaft has unusual vibration
Remedy / Action: Inspect the bearing and shaft; replace defective bearing parts and check alignment before restart
Measurable condition: Vibration velocity above 4.5 mm/s RMS (ISO 10816 Class III zone C limit)
Source: StepperOnline, “Gearbox - Troubleshooting Guide,” updated 2026, https://help.omc-stepperonline.com/hc/s/articles/gearbox-troubleshooting-guide

Symptom: Gearbox housing vibrates more than usual
Remedy / Action: Verify alignment and mounting and correct them as specified
Measurable condition: Vibration velocity above 4.5 mm/s RMS (ISO 10816 Class III zone C limit)
Source: StepperOnline, “Gearbox - Troubleshooting Guide,” updated 2026, https://help.omc-stepperonline.com/hc/s/articles/gearbox-troubleshooting-guide

Symptom: Gearbox housing vibrates more than usual
Remedy / Action: Verify the installation and reinstall as specified
Measurable condition: Vibration velocity above 4.5 mm/s RMS (ISO 10816 Class III zone C limit)
Source: StepperOnline, “Gearbox - Troubleshooting Guide,” updated 2026, https://help.omc-stepperonline.com/hc/s/articles/gearbox-troubleshooting-guide

Symptom: Gearbox housing vibrates more than usual
Cause / Fault: Unbalance or bent shaft (high vibration at 1x shaft speed)
Remedy / Action: Check balance and shaft straightness; correct or replace
Measurable condition: High vibration at 1x shaft frequency
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Gearbox housing vibrates more than usual
Cause / Fault: Angular misalignment or mechanical looseness (high vibration at 2x shaft speed)
Remedy / Action: Realign the coupling to tolerance; tighten loose parts
Measurable condition: High vibration at 2x shaft frequency
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Gearbox housing vibrates more than usual
Cause / Fault: Gear mesh wear or eccentric gear (gear mesh frequency dominant)
Remedy / Action: Compare the spectrum to the baseline; inspect the gears
Measurable condition: High vibration at gear mesh frequency and harmonics
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Gearbox housing vibrates more than usual
Remedy / Action: Check the foundation, hold-down torque and grout condition
Measurable condition: Sudden vibration increase of more than 50% above baseline
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Bearing defect frequencies in the vibration spectrum
Cause / Fault: Outer race, inner race, ball or cage fault on a specific bearing
Remedy / Action: Take an envelope spectrum, identify the bearing and plan its replacement
Measurable condition: Bearing defect frequencies present in the spectrum
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Lubricating oil appears around the shaft seal
Cause / Fault: Shaft oil seal worn or damaged
Remedy / Action: Locate the leak source, replace the seal and correct the underlying cause
Source: Ergenc, “Gearbox: troubleshooting step by step,” updated 2026, https://www.ergenc.com/en/kennis/maintenance/gearbox-troubleshooting-step-by-step/

Symptom: Lubricating oil appears around the shaft seal
Cause / Fault: Excess internal pressure from a blocked breather
Remedy / Action: Check the breather first and clean or replace it
Source: Ergenc, “Gearbox: troubleshooting step by step,” updated 2026, https://www.ergenc.com/en/kennis/maintenance/gearbox-troubleshooting-step-by-step/; Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Lubricating oil appears around the shaft seal
Cause / Fault: Shaft surface damaged at the seal contact area
Remedy / Action: Inspect and repair or replace the shaft before fitting a new seal
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Oil seeps from the joint between housing sections
Remedy / Action: Clean to pinpoint the leak; replace or reseal the joint to the maker instructions
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Oil seeps from the joint between housing sections
Remedy / Action: Check and re-torque the hold-down bolts
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Oil seeps from the joint between housing sections
Cause / Fault: Mating surface damaged or housing distorted
Remedy / Action: Inspect the joint; repair or replace the damaged parts
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Oil is expelled or leaks around the breather
Remedy / Action: Drain to the correct oil level
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Oil is expelled or leaks around the breather
Remedy / Action: Clean or replace the breather
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Oil is expelled or leaks around the breather
Remedy / Action: Take a sample for water and foam tendency; correct the oil condition and check the grade
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Oil is expelled or leaks around the breather
Remedy / Action: Find and remove the water-entry route; renew the oil
Measurable condition: Water content above 500 ppm in mineral oil
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Oil seeps at a drain plug or fitting
Cause / Fault: Damaged threads or missing sealing washer
Remedy / Action: Replace the sealing washer and use sealant rated for the lubricant
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Oil seeps at a drain plug or fitting
Remedy / Action: Repair or replace the damaged part
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Gearbox casing or oil temperature becomes unusually high
Cause / Fault: Oil level too low (reduced lubrication and increased friction)
Remedy / Action: Check the level using the specified method and refill with approved oil to the maker mark
Measurable condition: Sump oil temperature above 200 F (about 93 C); normal range is 130-180 F
Source: Ergenc, “Gearbox: troubleshooting step by step,” updated 2026, https://www.ergenc.com/en/kennis/maintenance/gearbox-troubleshooting-step-by-step/; Cotta, “Technical Information and Resources – Gearbox Overheating,” n.d., https://cotta.com/downloads-online-forms/technical-information-faq/

Symptom: Gearbox casing or oil temperature becomes unusually high
Remedy / Action: Confirm the correct lubricant is in the unit
Measurable condition: Sump oil temperature above 200 F (about 93 C); normal range is 130-180 F
Source: Ergenc, “Gearbox: troubleshooting step by step,” updated 2026, https://www.ergenc.com/en/kennis/maintenance/gearbox-troubleshooting-step-by-step/; Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Gearbox casing or oil temperature becomes unusually high
Remedy / Action: Confirm the load is within the rated limit; check the service factor
Measurable condition: Sump oil temperature above 200 F (about 93 C); normal range is 130-180 F
Source: Ergenc, “Gearbox: troubleshooting step by step,” updated 2026, https://www.ergenc.com/en/kennis/maintenance/gearbox-troubleshooting-step-by-step/; Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Gearbox casing or oil temperature becomes unusually high
Cause / Fault: Poor cooling (cooler fouled or low coolant flow)
Remedy / Action: Inspect and clean the cooler; verify coolant flow and valve operation
Measurable condition: Sump oil temperature above 200 F (about 93 C); normal range is 130-180 F
Source: Ergenc, “Gearbox: troubleshooting step by step,” updated 2026, https://www.ergenc.com/en/kennis/maintenance/gearbox-troubleshooting-step-by-step/; Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Gearbox casing or oil temperature becomes unusually high
Remedy / Action: Assess bearing condition and replace if damaged
Measurable condition: Sump oil temperature above 200 F (about 93 C); normal range is 130-180 F
Source: Ergenc, “Gearbox: troubleshooting step by step,” updated 2026, https://www.ergenc.com/en/kennis/maintenance/gearbox-troubleshooting-step-by-step/; Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Gearbox casing or oil temperature becomes unusually high
Remedy / Action: Drain to the correct level
Measurable condition: Sump oil temperature above 200 F (about 93 C); normal range is 130-180 F
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Gearbox casing or oil temperature becomes unusually high
Cause / Fault: Lubricant degradation or internal wear increasing friction (temperature creeping up over weeks)
Remedy / Action: Pull an oil sample for viscosity and acid number; clean the cooler
Measurable condition: Acid number rise of 0.5 or more above the new-oil baseline
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: One bearing housing much hotter than the others
Remedy / Action: Thermograph all bearing locations; plan an inspection of the hot bearing
Measurable condition: One bearing housing 30 F or more hotter than its sister bearing
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: One bearing housing much hotter than the others
Remedy / Action: Check lubricant supply to that location
Measurable condition: One bearing housing 30 F or more hotter than its sister bearing
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: One bearing housing much hotter than the others
Remedy / Action: Check alignment and load distribution
Measurable condition: One bearing housing 30 F or more hotter than its sister bearing
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Oil looks milky or cloudy
Remedy / Action: Eliminate the water-entry route, then drain and replace the oil per the maintenance manual
Measurable condition: Water content above 500 ppm in mineral oil
Source: Ergenc, “Gearbox: troubleshooting step by step,” updated 2026, https://www.ergenc.com/en/kennis/maintenance/gearbox-troubleshooting-step-by-step/

Symptom: Metallic particles in the drained oil or oil sample
Cause / Fault: Gear or bearing surfaces wearing or breaking down
Remedy / Action: Take an oil sample, find the source and arrange an internal inspection; replace damaged parts
Measurable condition: Rising iron together with rising PQ index
Source: Ergenc, “Gearbox: troubleshooting step by step,” updated 2026, https://www.ergenc.com/en/kennis/maintenance/gearbox-troubleshooting-step-by-step/; Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Pitting or scoring visible on gear teeth on inspection
Remedy / Action: Review lubrication and load; plan gear repair or replacement
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Pitting or scoring visible on gear teeth on inspection
Remedy / Action: Confirm the oil grade and level; correct the lubrication
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Pitting or scoring visible on gear teeth on inspection
Cause / Fault: Misalignment (wear concentrated at one end of the tooth face)
Remedy / Action: Realign the gear train and coupling
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Gearbox runs roughly or becomes noisy after installation
Remedy / Action: Check the setup against the installation manual and correct it before returning to service
Source: Ho Hsing Precision Industry Co., Ltd., “Gearbox Operation Manual,” circa 2018, https://www.k-online.de/vis-content/event-k2019/exh-k2019.2626823/K-2019-Ho-Hsing-Precision-Industry-Co.-Ltd.-Product-k2019.2626823-PWxD5DoNSfCiO7cs8gQu1A.pdf

Symptom: Gearbox runs roughly or becomes noisy after installation
Remedy / Action: Check and tighten the mounting
Source: Ho Hsing Precision Industry Co., Ltd., “Gearbox Operation Manual,” circa 2018, https://www.k-online.de/vis-content/event-k2019/exh-k2019.2626823/K-2019-Ho-Hsing-Precision-Industry-Co.-Ltd.-Product-k2019.2626823-PWxD5DoNSfCiO7cs8gQu1A.pdf

Symptom: Gearbox runs roughly or becomes noisy after installation
Remedy / Action: Check the coupling and shaft alignment against the installation manual
Source: Ho Hsing Precision Industry Co., Ltd., “Gearbox Operation Manual,” circa 2018, https://www.k-online.de/vis-content/event-k2019/exh-k2019.2626823/K-2019-Ho-Hsing-Precision-Industry-Co.-Ltd.-Product-k2019.2626823-PWxD5DoNSfCiO7cs8gQu1A.pdf

Symptom: Loss of output torque under normal input
Remedy / Action: Shut down and inspect; do not raise input torque to recover output
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Loss of output torque under normal input
Remedy / Action: Shut down and inspect the coupling
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Loss of output torque under normal input
Remedy / Action: Shut down and inspect; replace the shaft or key
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Output speed varies with constant input
Remedy / Action: Shut down; inspect through covers and plan a teardown
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Output speed varies with constant input
Remedy / Action: Shut down; inspect and replace the gears
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Output speed varies with constant input
Remedy / Action: Shut down; inspect and replace the element
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Output shaft axial movement
Remedy / Action: Measure with a dial indicator and replace the thrust bearing
Measurable condition: End float above the maker allowable value
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Output shaft axial movement
Cause / Fault: Locating shoulder wear or excessive internal axial play
Remedy / Action: Measure end float against the maker specification and repair
Measurable condition: End float above the maker allowable value
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Output shaft radial runout above tolerance
Remedy / Action: Recheck alignment; replace the shaft
Measurable condition: Runout above the maker tolerance
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Output shaft radial runout above tolerance
Remedy / Action: Plan bearing replacement
Measurable condition: Runout above the maker tolerance
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Output shaft radial runout above tolerance
Remedy / Action: Inspect and replace the coupling; recheck alignment
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Unit will not turn or jams on start
Cause / Fault: Locked rotor from internal failure or foreign object
Remedy / Action: Do not force the unit; open and inspect
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Unit will not turn or jams on start
Cause / Fault: Oil too cold for the viscosity grade
Remedy / Action: Allow the oil to warm or use the correct grade; prelube
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: Unit will not turn or jams on start
Remedy / Action: Verify brake release before starting
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting

Symptom: High motor current or thermal trips
Cause / Fault: Overload (service factor too low for the actual duty)
Remedy / Action: Review the service factor against actual duty and check for process changes
Measurable condition: Motor current above nameplate rating
Source: Malloy Electric, “Industrial Gearbox Troubleshooting Guide,” n.d., https://www.malloyelectric.com/gearbox-troubleshooting
